thread:
Evan: hey all :wave: i'm Evan, just joined the runtime team. trying to build the runtime from source inside a container and getting a linker/runtime error about missing libcuda / cuInit. using ubuntu:22.04 base with CUDA 12.2 installed in the image. any quick pointers for a day-0 newbie?

Tara: welcome Evan :tada: quick Qs — are you running the container with the NVIDIA runtime / nvidia-container-toolkit? often this is a host vs container driver mismatch. can you paste the exact docker run line and the error snippet?

Evan: thanks Tara. here's the docker run and the tail of the error:
```bash
docker run --rm -it my-runtime-build:dev /bin/bash
# inside container
cmake --build .
[ 84%] Linking CXX shared library libinfruntime.so
/usr/bin/ld: error: undefined reference to `cuInit'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
I also did `ldd build/libinfruntime.so` and it shows `libcuda.so.1 => not found`

devops-bot: CI: docker image my-runtime-build:dev created (tag 2025-11-04), no runtime detected.

Mira: hey Evan — if ldd shows libcuda not found that usually means the host's driver libs aren't being injected into the container. Two common fixes: (1) run with the NVIDIA container runtime / toolkit so libs are mounted automatically, or (2) bind-mount the host libcuda dir into the container (not ideal). can you run `nvidia-smi` on the host and inside the container and paste outputs? also `docker info | grep -i runtime`

Evan: host nvidia-smi:
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.54       Driver Version: 535.54       CUDA Version: 12.2     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
inside container `nvidia-smi` returns "command not found" (docker image didn't have nvidia-utils) and `docker info` shows no runtimes configured. I tried bind-mounting `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1` into `/usr/local/cuda/lib64` but the linker still fails.

Tara: sounds like Docker Desktop / engine isn't configured to use the nvidia runtime. if you're on a linux host install `nvidia-container-toolkit` and configure dockerd to include the `nvidia` runtime, then `--gpus=all` should work. if you're on WSL2 / Docker Desktop there are extra gotchas — Desktop may not expose host drivers to the distro. also ensure you aren't mixing toolkit-installed CUDA inside container with host driver that doesn't match — driver >= CUDA minor is required.

Mira: example docker run we use for builds so the libs are available:
```bash
docker run --gpus=all --rm -it \n  -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all \n  --init \n  -v /usr/local/cuda:/usr/local/cuda:ro \n  my-runtime-build:dev bash
```
If `--gpus=all` fails, check `sudo systemctl restart docker` after installing nvidia-container-toolkit. If you must bind mount, mount the whole lib dir: `-v /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/:/host-lib/` and add `/host-lib` to `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` before building.

Evan: thanks — i'm on a Mac using Docker Desktop with WSL backend (remote linux VM). I noticed Docker Desktop had an older WSL distro registered that still had the old driver stack. switched Docker Desktop to use the host GPU passthrough and re-ran with `--gpus=all` and now `nvidia-smi` works inside the container. build is progressing past the linker step.

Tara: awesome, glad it was that WSL distro/passthrough mismatch — very common for laptop setups. for CI we vendor a small shim that verifies `nvidia-smi` in the build image early and fails fast with a helpful message if the runtime isn't present. happy to share that snippet if you want.

Evan: huge help, thanks both. would love the CI snippet when you have a moment. solved for now :thumbsup:

Mira: i'll paste the CI check in the eng-runtime shared snippets channel later — it's a 3-line bash check. welcome aboard again :wave:
